This isolates a finite-reference/nonfinite-native observation; the native implementation and cause are unproven.
Explicit BF16 boundary differs from full graph CastAvx/buffer/context behavior.
Original native seq_length/q_seq=4096 and cast absorption attributes are retained with actual tensor length64.
State rounded after each step is a secondary comparison, not a claim about SDK internal precision.
Values equal to the initial NaN sentinel do not individually establish a device write.
S1 uses the first timestep and the same zero initial state. It cannot establish accuracy for decay of a nonzero prior state.
S1 also enables hybrid_opt_token_backend=npu; this is not a comparison with identical provider options and sequence shape.
S64 -80 and -128 references coincide at FP64 precision only for these inputs; this is not general mathematical equivalence.
A finite S1 does not establish an efficient or accurate full-model Loop implementation.
No old report or original probe was changed.
The Loop schedules and slices on CPU and invokes native NPU LinearAttention 64 times.
BF16 state is carried each timestep; bit equality with batched prefill is not asserted.
These are synthetic data, not actual layer14 captures. Actual model diagnostic captures are excluded.
Wall times include setup and capture and do not measure native operator latency alone.
This establishes these fixtures only, not all model layers or full16K operation.
Native internal overflow is a hypothesis; the closed native implementation was not identified.
Native finite/error values are observations, not a benchmark acceptance threshold or a full-model quality claim.
Host Loop, Gather and scan assembly use CPU; native LinearAttention uses the NPU.
Public repro_native.py is CPU-mocked, not NPU-validated. Original observations used the per-case original_runner_sha256.
